gap: No result ChatGPT got states how much power an RV inverter draws just by being switched on. Victron publishes 13 W for its MultiPlus-II 12/3000 (3 W in Search mode), and Renogy rates the 2000W UPS model ChatGPT showed as a card at under 18 W. Left on for 24 hours, 18 W is about 432 Wh (about 36 Ah from a 12 V bank), which is 60% of the 720 Wh/day example budget in the Victron sizing article ChatGPT cited.
standout_why: Victron's cited article 'How to Size a Solar System for Your RV' (2026-05-04) sizes a 720 Wh/day budget and only says to add 10–15% for inverter losses. It gives no inverter idle draw, no inverter sizing and no product prices. The other cited page, Renogy's 'RV Inverter Installation Guide', came back as navigation only, with no models, prices or idle figures in the readable text. The rvtime.com 2026 guide (rank 8) wouldn't open (SSL certificate error), so I couldn't compare against it. ChatGPT's answer says '3,000W' for 3000W-class units without separating VA from W, and gives no idle draw.
decides: The finding backs ChatGPT's 2,000 W starting pick but adds a condition: in a solar RV, the inverter's own idle draw (13–18 W, or 3 W in Victron's Search mode) can use more of the daily budget than small loads do. A shopper who leaves the inverter on should pick a unit with a published search or power-saving mode, or switch it off. The finding also corrects the '3000' label on the Victron MultiPlus-II 12/3000: that is 3,000 VA, which is 2,400 W continuous at 25 °C. The REGO card's price has also gone up from the $949 ChatGPT showed to $989.99 on Renogy's store today.
